newsitem.title: USA: Conoco /PdVSA oil project to offer $700M bond.
newsitem.headline: Conoco /PdVSA oil project to offer $700M bond.

text.p: The $2.2 billion Petrozuata oil project, a joint venture between Dupont Co and state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA), will begin a "roadshow" with investors Friday ahead of a planned bond offering of around $700 million in the U.S. market, a source involved in the venture said Thursday.

The bond offering originally had been planned for $300 million to $500 million but a higher-than-expected "investment grade" rating from at least one of the main credit rating agencies encouraged project participants to raise a larger amount.
Moody's Investors Service Inc will rate the bonds Baa1, two grades above the minimum investment grade rating of Baa3 and significantly above the Venezuela's sovereign Ba2 grade.

Petrozuata is the first of six projects worth a total $15 billion to upgrade extra-heavy Venezuelan crude oil to more marketable "synthetic" crude. The progress of Petrozuata, particularly at the financing stage, is being closely watched as a bellwether for the other five projects.
The structure of the Petrozuata deal is unusual in that there is an "offshore" trust set up which puts it at arms length from the government and limits the financial risks.

Of the $2.2 billion cost of the project, about 40 percent is expected to be equity and 60 percent debt. Apart from the bond offering, Petrozuata will raise loan capital from banks via some form of senior debt financing.
The partners, Conoco and the Maraven operating unit of PdVSA, earlier this year named CS First Boston and Citibank as lead and co-lead, respectively, of the proposed bond offering.
Credit Suisse, ING Barings, Nationsbank and Union Bank of Switzerland are arrangers of the commercial bank loan.

The project will upgrade the extra-heavy crude from the country's sprawling Orinoco Tar Belt, converting about 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of the heavy stuff into 104,000 bpd of 21 API gravity synthetic crude for export to the U.S. The Tar Belt, Faja in Spanish, contains an estimated 270 billion barrels of recoverable reserves.
